blocks.value: **An interface is used to specify methods that a class must implement.** It contains headings for a number of public methods, and should include comments describing them.
Different classes can implement the same interface:
public class ClassName implements InterfaceName1, InterfaceName2 { }
public class Rectangle implements Countable, Measurable { }
Now polymorphism works across **completely unrelated** classes:
`Rectangle` and `Circle` share no base class. The interface is the only thing they have in common, and it is enough.
The description above (headings only) matches Java 7 and your handout's era. Modern interfaces may also contain **`default`** methods with a body and **`static`** methods:
This was added so interfaces could gain new methods without breaking every existing implementer. Exam questions will likely follow the older definition; real code you meet will use both.
